name: United monarchy of Israel
description: Saul, David and Solomon, before the kingdom divided (c. 931 BC). Reign lengths are given in the Bible; absolute dates follow from the division date.
citation: 1 Samuel–1 Kings 11; Wikipedia, 'Kings of Israel and Judah' (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Kingdom of Judah
description: The southern kingdom, ruled by David's line from Jerusalem until the Babylonian conquest (587/586 BC). Scholars reconstruct the regnal years differently; coregencies (a son reigning beside his father) explain many of the Bible's synchronisms.
citation: Thiele (1983); Galil (1996); Albright (1945) — see chronology systems

name: Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)
description: The northern kingdom, from Jeroboam I to the Assyrian conquest of Samaria (722 BC), ruled by a succession of dynasties.
citation: Thiele (1983); Galil (1996); Albright (1945) — see chronology systems

name: Egypt (pharaohs named in the Bible)
description: Pharaohs the Old Testament names: Shishak, Tirhakah, Necho and Hophra.
citation: Wikipedia, 'List of pharaohs' and the kings' articles (CC BY-SA 4.0); Egyptian dates are approximate

name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
description: Assyria dominated Israel and Judah from Tiglath-Pileser III (745 BC) until its fall; it destroyed Samaria in 722 BC. Dates from the Assyrian eponym lists are exact to the year until the 630s BC.
citation: Assyrian eponym canon; Wikipedia, 'List of Assyrian kings' (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
description: Babylon took over Assyria's empire, made Judah a vassal after Carchemish (605 BC), destroyed Jerusalem (587/586 BC) and fell to Cyrus in 539 BC.
citation: Babylonian Chronicles; Parker & Dubberstein, Babylonian Chronology (1956); Wikipedia, 'List of kings of Babylon' (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Achaemenid Persian Empire
description: Cyrus let the exiles return (538 BC); Judah was the Persian province of Yehud until Alexander.

name: Alexander the Great
description: Alexander conquered the Persian Empire; Judaea passed to him in 332 BC.

name: Ptolemaic Egypt
description: The Macedonian dynasty of Egypt; it ruled Judaea from 301 BC until the battle of Panium (200 BC). Joint reigns and civil wars make some later dates overlap.

name: Seleucid Empire
description: The Macedonian dynasty of Syria and Mesopotamia; it ruled Judaea from 200 BC. Antiochus IV's persecution set off the Maccabean revolt; rival claimants overlap after 150 BC.

name: Hasmonean Judaea
description: The Maccabees and their descendants: leaders of the revolt, then high priests and ethnarchs, and from 104 BC kings.
citation: 1 Maccabees; Josephus, Antiquities 12–14; Wikipedia, 'Hasmonean dynasty' (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Herodian dynasty
description: Herod the Great and his descendants, client kings and tetrarchs under Rome.

name: Roman governors of Judaea
description: Prefects (AD 6–41) and procurators (AD 44–66) of the Roman province of Judaea. Exact years of several governors are inferred from Josephus and are approximate.
citation: Josephus, Antiquities 18–20 and War 2; Wikipedia, 'List of Roman governors of Judaea' (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Other Roman governors in the New Testament
description: Roman governors named in Luke and Acts outside Judaea.
citation: Wikipedia, 'Quirinius' and 'Gallio' (CC BY-SA 4.0); the Delphi (Gallio) inscription

name: High priests (Second Temple)
description: High priests in Jerusalem whose terms are reasonably dated: the Hellenistic crisis (2 Maccabees) and the appointees of Herod and Rome (Josephus). The Hasmonean rulers, who were also high priests, are listed under Hasmonean Judaea.
citation: 2 Maccabees; Josephus, Antiquities 15–20; Wikipedia, 'List of High Priests of Israel' (CC BY-SA 4.0)

name: Roman emperors
description: From Augustus to Theodosius I. Co-emperors overlap; usurpers and short-lived claimants are left out.
citation: Kienast, Römische Kaisertabelle; Wikipedia, 'List of Roman emperors' (CC BY-SA 4.0)
